doc.name: A — cosmetics catalogue, steam and heat, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: matte lipstick bullet
Category: cosmetics
Shot programme: steam and heat
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You are the visual lead responsible for this cosmetics product library. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the extreme wide set in a steam and heat treatment.

SUBJECT. A matte lipstick bullet. Copy the product from the reference verbatim in form and finish. If a detail is unreadable in the reference, keep it neutral rather than inventing one.

CAMERA. Wide frame with the product small in a large, deliberately empty set. Shoot on a probe macro lens at f/11, framing for a shallow out-of-focus foreground element occluding the lower third.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with scrim-diffused midday daylight, one stop under the ambient. Stage the product on or against hand-thrown ceramic, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a punchy saturated candy palette with hard primaries. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Your entire reply is the prompt itself: one dense paragraph, no title, no quotation marks, no trailing notes.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.
